title: Component props
summary: Props are inputs passed from a parent component to a child component.
whenToUse: Use props when a child component needs data or configuration from the component that renders it.
do: Pass only the data a child component needs.
Destructure props when it makes the component easier to scan.
Keep props read-only inside the child component.
dont: Do not mutate props inside the child component.
Do not pass a large object when a few explicit props would be clearer.

codeSnippets.title: Pass props to a child
codeSnippets.description: The parent provides values, and the child renders them.
codeSnippets.explanation: Profile receives name and role as props and uses them in its JSX.

commonMistake: Trying to change props inside the child component instead of asking the parent to update state.
interviewQuestion: Are props mutable inside a component?
interviewAnswer: No. Props are read-only from the child component's point of view; state changes should happen in the owner component.

courseReference.notes: Components receive data from parent components to render menu content.

title: The children prop
summary: children contains the JSX placed between a component's opening and closing tags.
whenToUse: Use children for wrapper components, layout components, reusable boxes, and flexible composition.
do: Use children when the caller should decide the nested content.
Keep wrapper components focused on structure or styling.
Combine children with regular props when both are useful.
dont: Do not create many narrow content props when children would be simpler.
Do not assume children is always plain text; it can be any React node.

codeSnippets.title: Wrap flexible content
codeSnippets.description: A wrapper component can render whatever is placed inside it.
codeSnippets.explanation: Card controls the outer section, while the caller controls the nested content.

commonMistake: Creating many specific props when children would make the component more flexible.
interviewQuestion: What is the children prop used for?
interviewAnswer: children lets a component receive and render nested JSX, making composition more flexible.

courseReference.notes: Wrapper and button components are useful places to practice composition.
